exact_statement: For every finite positive width-two graph prime table, positive globally packing-feasible lambda, nonempty k-gate subset T, and certified L>0 with sum_T lambda<=L, the conditioned used-gate root-index law obeys p_lambda(T)<=1/[(1+4k/L)^k-(4k/L)^k]. For k>=2 this strictly improves the previous min(1,4^(1-k)L^(k-1)/k^k) cap. It is a sharp supremum when equal weights L/k on T are feasible and the table is allowed positive outside weights tending to zero. For every pair of incident gates i,j in any such table, singleton probabilities p_i,p_j and pair probability r obey p_i*p_j>=4r(p_i+p_j), equivalently [[p_i-4r,4r],[4r,p_j-4r]] is positive semidefinite, yielding t^2*p_i+p_j>=4(t+1)^2*r for every rational t>=0. For exactly two incident gates, positivity, normalization and this cone characterize all feasible root laws. The positive normalized law (2/3,5/18,1/18) satisfies all sharp individual caps and both individual lambda<=1 bounds but violates packing: recovered lambda=(4/5,1/3), determinant=-2/81, t=1/2 cut=-1/18. This is a root-relaxation falsifier, not a Boolean spectral or variational-cost counterexample. On the frozen 67 full-family graph references, new cap LP gaps improve strictly in61 cases; all31 frozen star sizes m2..32 improve strictly. No universal coding-cost payment or FEI solution follows.
